Sit straight on a mat with your right knee bent to the left side and your right foot behind you. Put your left foot against your right thigh. 

Keep your hips grounded. Place your hands on the floor for support.

Engage your abs to bring your torso back to the sitting position. Then lift your left arm and curve your body to the right side.

Repeat the exercise.

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your back straight.
Breathe naturally.
Please do not lift your shoulder as you curve.
This exercise stretches your obliques, shoulders, and inner thighs.

1450.name: MERMAID RIGHT
1450.introduce:
Sit straight on a mat with your left knee bent to the right side and your left foot behind you. Put your right foot against your left thigh. 

Keep your hips grounded. Place your hands on the floor for support.

Engage your abs to bring your torso back to the sitting position. Then lift your right arm and curve your body to the left side.

Repeat the exercise.

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please put your left hand on the floor for some support.
Please keep your back straight.
Breathe naturally.
Please do not lift your shoulder as you curve.
Please let your right arm as close as much to your ear as you curve.
This exercise stretches your obliques, shoulders, and inner thighs.

3343.name: CROSS TAP SIDE SWING
3343.introduce: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Alternately tap one foot across the front of your body to the opposite side while swinging your arms side to side. Breathe naturally with the rhythm.

tips.text: Let the arms swing freely — don't force the motion.
Breathe naturally with the rhythm of your steps.
This is a great warm-up that gently fires up your arms and legs.

3344.name: BACK TAP DIAGONAL REACH
3344.introduce: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Alternately tap one foot diagonally behind your body to the opposite side while swinging your arms upward to the sides. Breathe naturally with the rhythm.

tips.text: Keep the supporting leg stable as you tap behind.
Breathe naturally as the arms sweep up.
Keep your neck relaxed.
This exercise activates your arms and legs.

3345.name: MARCHING PALM PRESS
3345.introduce:
Stand with your hands at chest level, palms facing forward. March in place.

As you march, press both palms forward, then pull them back. Keep your chest lifted and land softly with each step.

Breathe steadily throughout the movement.

tips.text: Keep the palms strong as you push.
Engage your core to drive each press forward.
Let your feet land softly.
Breathe steadily.
This exercise warms up your shoulders and builds arm strength.

3346.name: TOE TAP OVERHEAD LIFT
3346.introduce:
Stand with feet hip-width apart.

Lightly tap your left toes forward, raising both arms overhead with palms facing each other.

Alternate sides smoothly and breathe naturally with the tempo.

tips.text: Avoid shrugging your shoulders as you raise your arms.
Inhale as you lift your arms, and exhale as you lower them.
A slightly faster tempo will help raise your heart rate.
This exercise opens up your chest and shoulders.

3347.name: HEEL KICK CURL
3347.introduce:
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Step the left foot out to the side as the right heel kicks back toward the glute.

At the same time, bend the elbows and lift both forearms in front of the chest with palms facing each other.

Alternate sides smoothly and breathe steadily through the rhythm.

tips.text: Squeeze your glute as you kick the heel back.
Tighten your core to keep the upper body steady.
Bend the elbows fully on each curl for a stronger contraction.
Breathe steadily through the rhythm.
This exercise works your hamstrings, glutes and biceps all at once.

3348.name: CROSS TAP OVERHEAD WIPER
3348.introduce:
Stand with arms raised overhead.

Cross-tap the left foot in front of the body to the right side, while both arms swing down together to the left like windshield wipers.

Alternate sides smoothly. Breathe naturally with the sweep.

tips.text: Keep the hips facing forward.
Use your waist to power the wiper motion.
Breathe naturally with each sweep.
You should feel both sides of your waist working evenly.
This exercise is excellent for trimming the waistline and obliques.

3349.name: QUICK MARCH SINGLE PALM PUSH
3349.introduce:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hands at chest height with palms facing forward.

March in place at a brisk tempo, pushing the opposite-side palm forward with each step.

Alternate left and right smoothly. Let your breath follow the pace — if it gets short, slow down and pace yourself.

tips.text: Stay tall through the chest as you march.
Pump the palms forward with intention, not floppy wrists.
Let the breath follow your pace — keep it natural.
If your breathing gets short, slow the tempo down.
This exercise raises the heart rate and boosts circulation quickly.

3350.name: KICKBACK AND ARM LIFT
3350.introduce:
Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width apart.

Lift the left leg back as your weight shifts onto the right foot, while the left arm sweeps forward and up overhead and the right arm swings naturally back.

Alternate sides smoothly and breathe naturally with the rhythm.

tips.text: Reach the arm long overhead — fingertips lifted to the sky.
Engage the core so the lower back doesn't arch.
Inhale as the leg lifts and the arm reaches up; exhale as they lower.
This exercise helps improve balance, posture, and full-body coordination.

3351.name: LUNGE STRETCH LEFT
3351.introduce:
Step the left leg forward into a low front lunge, both feet flat on the floor. Place the hands on the hips and lift the chest tall.

Gently pulse the hips forward, sinking deeper with each pulse to feel the stretch through the back leg and inner thighs.

Take slow, full breaths throughout. Use a wall or chair to help with balance if needed.

tips.text: Keep your front knee aligned over the ankle, not past the toes.
Square the hips forward and lift the chest tall.
Take slow, full breaths throughout.
Use a wall or chair for balance if needed.
This exercise stretches the legs and the hip flexor.

3352.name: FORWARD FOLD HAMSTRING STRETCH
3352.introduce:
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.

Extend the right leg forward with the heel on the floor, then fold the upper body over the front leg, sliding the hands down the leg to feel a stretch along the back of the thigh.

Rise tall, sweeping both arms overhead with palms facing each other.

Lower the arms and switch sides. Exhale as you fold, and inhale as you rise.

tips.text: Soften the knee of the front leg if your hamstrings feel too tight.
Fold from the hips, not the lower back.
Exhale as you fold, and inhale as you rise.
You should feel a comfortable pull, not a sharp pain.
This exercise stretches the hamstrings.

3353.name: LUNGE STRETCH RIGHT
3353.introduce:
Step the right leg forward into a low front lunge, both feet flat on the floor. Place the hands on the hips and lift the chest tall.

Gently pulse the hips forward, sinking deeper with each pulse to feel the stretch through the back leg and inner thighs.

Take slow, full breaths throughout. Use a wall or chair to help with balance if needed.

tips.text: Keep your front knee aligned over the ankle, not past the toes.
Square the hips forward and lift the chest tall.
Take slow, full breaths throughout.
Use a wall or chair for balance if needed.
This exercise stretches the legs and the hip flexor.

3354.name: TOE TAP OVERHEAD RING AND OPEN
3354.introduce:
Stand with feet hip-width apart. Alternate tapping your toes forward in a steady rhythm.

At the same time, open and close your arms horizontally at shoulder height 4 times.

Then raise both arms overhead, forming a soft circle with the arms, for 4 repetitions.

Breathe naturally with the movement.

tips.text: Keep the toe taps light and rhythmic — don't slap the floor.
Round the arms naturally, like holding a big balloon overhead.
Breathe naturally with the rhythm.
This exercise warms up the shoulders and legs.

3355.name: SIDE STEP SINGLE PALM PUSH
3355.introduce:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hands at chest height.

Step to the left and lightly tap the right toe in. At the same time, press the right palm forward at chest level while keeping the left hand near the chest.

Alternate sides smoothly. Breathe steadily with the movement.

tips.text: Keep a soft bend in the standing leg as you tap the toe in.
Press the palm all the way forward.
Breathe steadily as you step.
This exercise tones the arms and engages the inner and outer thighs.

3356.name: SIDE STEP SUN CIRCLE
3356.introduce:
Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width apart.

Step to the left and tap the right toe in. At the same time, sweep the right arm in a large circle upward across the front of the chest.

Alternate sides smoothly. Breathe naturally with the movement.

tips.text: Make the arm circle big — reach all the way up.
Keep the supporting leg soft and light.
Breathe naturally as the arm moves.
This exercise mobilizes the shoulders and boosts cardiovascular health.

3357.name: FRONT KICK BICEP CURL
3357.introduce:
Stand with feet hip-width apart.

Lightly kick the left leg forward while lifting the opposite arm with the elbow bent.
Alternate sides smoothly.

Breathe evenly with the movement. If your knee feels tender, lift the leg lower or switch to a steady march.

tips.text: Kick lightly — control matters more than height.
Keep the upper body lifted and the core engaged.
Avoid locking the supporting knee.
Breathe evenly through the movement.
This exercise strengthens the legs and improves upper-body coordination.

3358.name: HIGH KNEE BICEP CURL
3358.introduce:
Stand with feet hip-width apart.

Lift the left knee to hip height while lifting the opposite arm with the elbow bent.
Alternate sides smoothly.

Breathe evenly with the movement.

tips.text: Lift the knee with control, not momentum.
Tighten the abs to keep your balance.
Don't hunch the shoulders — stay upright.
Breathe to the rhythm of your steps.
This exercise builds core strength and improves balance.

3359.name: ARM CIRCLE LATERAL PUSH
3359.introduce:
Stand with feet hip-width apart. March in place while rolling the forearms in front of the chest for 6 counts.

Then tap the left toe out to the side as the left palm presses outward.

Alternate sides smoothly. Breathe steadily with the movement.

tips.text: Make the arm rolls smooth and continuous — avoid jerky movements.
Press the palm outward while keeping the wrist firm.
Breathe steadily with the rhythm.
This movement warms the shoulders and tones the legs.

3360.name: SIDE STEP BOW PULL
3360.introduce:
Hold both arms extended forward at chest height.

Step to the left and tap the right toe diagonally behind the body.

At the same time, pull the right elbow back while keeping the left arm extended forward.

Alternate sides smoothly. Breathe steadily with each side step.

tips.text: Keep both arms at chest height — don't let them droop.
Pull the elbow back strongly.
Breathe steadily with each side step.
This exercise strengthens the back and warms up the body.

3361.name: MARCHING TRIPLE PUSH
3361.introduce:
Stand with feet hip-width apart. March in place with soft, steady steps.

As you march, press both arms overhead, then out to the sides, then forward at chest level.

Repeat the sequence smoothly in rhythm. Breathe naturally with the movement.

tips.text: Stay focused on the sequence — up, out, then forward.
Push strongly through the palms in each direction.
Land the feet softly as you march.
Breathe naturally with the rhythm.
This exercise improves coordination and works the shoulders.

3364.name: FRONT BACK CLAP CIRCLE
3364.introduce:
Exhale and clap the palms in front of the body.

Inhale and open the arms wide behind you.

Continue flowing smoothly between the front clap and the backward arm sweep.

tips.text: Reach the arms back as far as your shoulders allow — don't force the movement.
Keep the chest lifted — don't hunch as the hands clap in front.
Exhale on the front clap and inhale as the arms sweep back.
This exercise opens the chest and improves shoulder mobility.

3366.name: CURTSY LUNGE OVERHEAD PRESS
3366.introduce:
Inhale and reach both arms high overhead.

Exhale and step the left foot diagonally back into a curtsy lunge while pulling the elbows down.

Inhale to return to standing and reach the arms overhead.

Alternate sides smoothly.

tips.text: Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
Inhale to reach up, and exhale to pull down.
This exercise tones the legs, glutes, and shoulders together.

3367.name: CURTSY LUNGE SPIRAL TWIST
3367.introduce:
Reach both arms forward at chest level with the palms facing each other.

Exhale, rotate the torso to the left and step the left foot diagonally back into a curtsy lunge as the left arm opens wide to the side.

Inhale to return to center. Alternate sides smoothly.

tips.text: Keep the front knee aligned with the toes.
Exhale into the twist, and inhale to return.
This exercise improves balance and spinal mobility.

3369.name: CROSS TAP OVERHEAD SWEEP
3369.introduce: Tap the left foot diagonally behind the body to the right as both arms sweep together in a large circular motion from left to right overhead.\n\nAlternate sides smoothly, breathing naturally with each sweep.

tips.text: Reach both arms overhead in a long diagonal sweep.
Let the side waist lengthen with each sweep.
Breathe naturally with each sweep.
This exercise stretches the side body and improves shoulder mobility.

3372.name: MARCHING CHEST FLY
3372.introduce:
Hold the forearms up at shoulder height with the elbows bent and palms facing forward.

Exhale, lift the left knee and bring the forearms together in front of the chest.

Inhale, lower the knee and open the arms wide to the sides.

Alternate sides smoothly.

tips.text: Open the chest fully and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Inhale as the arms open and exhale as the arms close.
This exercise opens the chest and mobilizes the hips.

3374.name: PALM TREE REACH UP
3374.introduce:
Stand shoulder-width apart with the fingers interlaced in front of the chest.

Inhale and extend both arms up through the centerline of the body, turning the palms upward overhead as the heels lift off the floor.

Exhale and lower the arms and heels back down.

tips.text: Reach up tall — feel the whole body lengthen.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears.
Inhale to expand upward, and exhale to release back down.
This exercise lengthens the spine and strengthens the calves.

3381.name: CRANE KNEE TAP
3381.introduce:
Inhale and lift both arms straight overhead with fingers interlaced.

Exhale and lift the left knee toward the chest as the hands lower to meet the front of the knee.

Inhale to return. Alternate sides smoothly.

tips.text: Reach the arms tall before lowering — feel the whole body lengthen.
Keep the supporting leg slightly soft, not locked.
Inhale as the arms reach up, and exhale as the knee meets them.
This exercise builds core strength and improves balance.

3382.name: CROSS REACH BALANCE
3382.introduce:
Stand tall with both arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.

Lift the left knee as the right hand reaches down toward the left ankle.

Return to standing and alternate sides smoothly.

Breathe naturally throughout the movement.

tips.text: Keep the standing leg slightly soft for stability.
Don't force the knee higher — let the hand come down to meet the leg.
Breathe naturally throughout.
This exercise challenges balance and opens the side body.

3383.name: EAGLE WING PULSE
3383.introduce:
Bend both arms at chest height with the elbows pointing outward.

Exhale, pulling the elbows back to open the chest.

Then inhale, extending the arms straight out at shoulder height and pull them back.

Alternate between the bent-arm and straight-arm patterns.

tips.text: Squeeze the shoulder blades together with each pull.
Keep the chest lifted — don't arch the lower back.
Coordinate the breath with the movement.
This exercise opens the chest and helps counter slouching from desk work.

3384.name: WIDE STANCE SIDE REACH
3384.introduce:
Stand wider than shoulder-width apart with both arms reaching overhead and the elbows softly bent.

Exhale and bend the right knee slightly while extending the left leg straight, lifting the left toes upward.

At the same time, reach the left hand toward the left leg.

Inhale to return and alternate sides smoothly.

tips.text: Keep the bent knee tracking over the toes.
Reach the top arm long to lengthen the side waist.
Inhale to rise and exhale into the side bend.
This exercise strengthens the legs and stretches the inner thigh.

3386.name: SCORPION OPPOSITE REACH
3386.introduce:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and extend both arms out to the sides at shoulder height.

Exhale as you bend the right knee and kick the heel back toward the glutes. At the same time, the left hand reaches back toward the right foot.

Inhale to return and alternate sides smoothly.

tips.text: Keep the standing leg slightly soft and the core engaged for balance.
Reach the hand back naturally, but don't force it to touch the foot.
Inhale to stand tall, and exhale as you kick back.
This exercise improves balance and activates the legs and glutes.

3389.name: BACK STEP ARMS OVERHEAD
3389.introduce:
Start with feet hip-width apart.

Inhale and step the right foot back with the toes touching down, sweeping both arms up and overhead in a long extension.

Exhale to return. Alternate sides smoothly, lengthening from the back heel through the lifted fingertips.

tips.text: Keep both arms reaching tall — feel the line from back heel to fingertips.
Keep the chest lifted.
Inhale as you reach up, and exhale as you return.
This opens the front body and improves balance.

3390.name: OUTER KICK BALANCE
3390.introduce:
Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width apart.

Clap the hands in front of the chest. Lift the left foot out to the side as the left hand reaches down to touch it.

Return and alternate sides smoothly. Breathe naturally with the rhythm.

tips.text: Engage the core to stay tall as the leg lifts.
Keep the standing leg slightly soft for balance.
Breathe naturally with the rhythm.
This exercise improves coordination and activates the glutes.

3392.name: KNEE LIFT ARM WAVE
3392.introduce:
Stand shoulder-width apart with both arms extended forward at shoulder height.

Exhale and lift the left knee to hip height, sweeping both arms out to the left side.

Inhale to return. Alternate sides smoothly. Breathe steadily with the rhythm.

tips.text: Keep the core engaged so the knee lifts cleanly.
Keep the torso stable as the arms sweep side to side.
Breathe steadily with the rhythm.
This exercise improves balance and core stability.

3393.name: TWISTING REACH UP
3393.introduce:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides, palms facing backward.

Exhale, twist your torso to the left while lifting your arms up and back.

Inhale, return to the starting position. Switch sides to repeat.

tips.text: Engage your core to maintain stability.
Exhale as you twist. Inhale as you return to the center.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders.
This exercise mobilizes the spine.
This exercise activates your shoulders and core.

3394.name: ARM WAVE FLOW
3394.introduce:
Stand comfortably with your hands crossed in front of your belly, palms facing down.

Alternately lift each arm in a smooth wave-like motion in front of your body.

Breathe steadily and keep your shoulders relaxed.

tips.text: Keep the shoulders soft — don't tense up.
Let the arms ripple like a smooth wave.
Breathe steadily as the arms flow.
This exercise helps relax your shoulders and arms.

3395.name: OBLIQUE SIDE KNEE LIFT
3395.introduce:
Stand upright. Interlace your fingers behind your head with your elbows open wide.

Exhale, pull your left elbow down to the side and lift your left knee, bringing them as close together as possible.

Inhale, return to the starting position. Switch sides to repeat.

tips.text: Engage your core to maintain stability.
Exhale as you lift the knee, inhale as you lower it.
This exercise strengthens your core and legs.

3397.name: PALM KNEE TAP
3397.introduce:
Stand upright with your forearms in front of your chest, parallel to the floor, and palms facing down.

Exhale, lift your left knee to try to touch your left palm.

Inhale, lower the leg down. Switch sides to repeat.

tips.text: Engage your core to maintain stability.
Keep the upper body tall as the knee lifts.
Exhale as you lift the knee, inhale as you lower it.
This exercise strengthens your core and legs.

3399.name: HEEL TAP PULL
3399.introduce:
Stand upright with your fists resting at your sides.

Exhale, tap your left heel diagonally forward to the left while pulling both fists toward your shoulders.

Inhale, return to the center. Switch sides to repeat.

tips.text: Tap the heel light and quick — don't press into the floor.
Exhale as you bend your elbows, inhale as you lower them.
Keep your weight on the back leg throughout the movement.
This exercise helps tone your arms and legs.

3401.name: CROSS TAP CIRCLE
3401.introduce:
Stand with your elbows bent at your sides, palms facing forward.

Alternately step one foot diagonally across the body, lightly tapping the floor with your toes.

At the same time, draw small circles with both arms while keeping the elbows bent.

Breathe naturally throughout.

tips.text: Keep your weight on the back leg throughout the movement.
Circle both arms smoothly in small circles.
Breathe naturally with the rhythm.
This exercise helps tone your shoulders and legs.

3402.name: SIDE BEND REACH STRETCH
3402.introduce:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing down.

Exhale, lean to the right, reaching the left arm overhead and across while the right hand touches the left waist.

Inhale, return to the starting position. Switch sides to repeat.

tips.text: Reach the top arm long to feel a long stretch through the side body.
Keep your hips stable.
Exhale as you lean to one side, and inhale as you return to center.
This exercise opens the side waist and shoulders.

3404.name: ELBOW PULL STRETCH
3404.introduce:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart. Interlace your fingers behind your head with your elbows open wide.

Pull the left elbow down gently to feel a soft stretch through the right arm and shoulder.

Breathe naturally and switch sides to repeat.

tips.text: Keep the chest lifted as you pull the elbow down.
Don't yank — feel a gentle, gradual stretch.
Breathe slowly and deeply throughout.
Keep the elbows open and the shoulders relaxed.
This exercise stretches the arms and shoulders.

3406.name: MARCHING HIP SWAY
3406.introduce:
Stand with your chest up and abs tight.

March in place, letting your hips sway from side to side with the rhythm.

At the same time, swing your arms naturally in coordination with your steps.

Breathe naturally throughout.

tips.text: Breathe naturally with the rhythm.
Keep your steps light and brisk, aiming for a flowing motion.
Make sure your arms and legs perform in coordination.
Land with your toes first, followed by your heel.
This exercise helps improve blood circulation and warm up.

3407.name: BACK STEP DIAGONAL REACH
3407.introduce:
Stand upright with your arms relaxed at your sides.

Exhale, step your left foot diagonally back to the left with only your toes touching the floor, while reaching your right hand overhead.

Inhale, return to the starting position. Switch sides to repeat.

tips.text: Engage your core to maintain balance and stability.
Always keep your back straight.
Exhale as you step back, inhale as you return.
This exercise stretches your arms, back, and legs.
This exercise helps improve balance.

3408.name: TWISTING UNDERARM PAT
3408.introduce:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart.

Exhale, twist your torso to the left, reach your left hand overhead, and lightly pat your left underarm with your right hand.

Inhale to return. Alternate sides to repeat in a smooth rhythm.

tips.text: Let the waist lead the twist.
Pat lightly with a springy touch.
Exhale to twist your torso, inhale to return to the center.
This exercise activates your shoulders, legs, and the side of your body.
This exercise stimulates the underarm meridians.

3409.name: TWISTING SHOULDER CIRCLE LEFT
3409.introduce:
Stand upright with your left arm bent at chest level, palm facing up, and the elbow relaxed.

Gently twist to the left as your left arm draws a large counterclockwise circle, then return to the starting position.

Breathe naturally and repeat.

tips.text: Perform the movement slowly and with control.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise warms up your shoulders and back.

3410.name: TWISTING SHOULDER CIRCLE RIGHT
3410.introduce:
Stand upright with your right arm bent at chest level, palm facing up, and the elbow relaxed.

Gently twist to the right as your right arm draws a large clockwise circle, then return to the starting position.

Breathe naturally and repeat.

tips.text: Perform the movement slowly and with control.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise warms up your shoulders and back.

3411.name: SPIRAL ROTATION
3411.introduce:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart.

Stack your hands together in front of your chest, elbows open to the sides.

Twist your torso from side to side as far as comfortable.

Breathe naturally throughout.

tips.text: Keep your chest lifted.
Let the waist drive the twist, not the shoulders.
Keep the elbows lifted and relaxed throughout.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise mobilizes the spine and stretches the obliques.

3414.name: PALM PUSH SWING
3414.introduce:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and keep your knees softly bent.

Push one palm to the sky while the opposite palm presses downward.

Gently shift your weight from side to side as your arms alternate.

Breathe naturally throughout.

tips.text: Reach long in both directions to feel a stretch through the side body.
Let the hips sway naturally.
Breathe steadily with the rhythm.
This exercise warms up your arms, shoulders, and core.

3415.name: SEE-SAW SWING
3415.introduce:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and keep your knees softly bent.

Alternately swing one arm upward while the opposite arm swings downward in front of your body.

At the same time, let your hips sway gently side to side with the rhythm.

Breathe naturally throughout.

tips.text: Breathe naturally.
Perform the movement smoothly and rhythmically.
Let your hips guide the rhythm.
This exercise helps activate your arms, shoulders, and hips.

3420.name: TWISTING CRANE
3420.introduce:
Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width apart and extend both arms out to the sides at shoulder height.

Slightly bend your knees and sweep your arms down.

As you rise, rotate your torso to the left and reach your left arm to the side while extending your right forward, forming an L.

Lower your arms, bend your knees, and bring your torso to the center.

Then return to the starting position and switch sides to repeat.

tips.text: Keep the shoulders relaxed.
Exhale as you twist your torso, and inhale as you return to center.
This exercise strengthens the legs, shoulders, and the side of the body.

3421.name: SPARROW LIFT
3421.introduce:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and rest your arms at your sides.

Exhale, lift your left knee as the right heel rises into a calf raise. Simultaneously, extend your left arm out to the side and reach your right arm overhead.

Inhale, return to the starting position and switch sides to repeat.

If your body allows, add a light bounce on the toe lift to challenge your heart and lungs.

tips.text: Lift the knee with control.
Engage your core to help maintain balance and stability.
Exhale as you lift the knee and arms. Inhale as you return to the starting position.
This exercise challenges balance and builds full-body coordination.
This exercise activates your shoulders and legs.

3422.name: STAMINA STEP
3422.introduce:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and lift both arms overhead, palms facing each other.

Alternately lift each heel while keeping your toes on the floor.

Breathe naturally and move in a steady marching rhythm.

tips.text: Lift the heels evenly — don't shift weight too far.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders.
Breathe naturally with the pace.
This exercise builds calf and core strength.
Slow the tempo if you feel rushed.

3423.name: SWALLOW WALK
3423.introduce:
Stand tall and raise your arms overhead from the sides.

Exhale, hinge at your hips, and step one foot forward with only the heels landed, while sweeping both arms back.

Inhale, return to the starting position and switch legs to repeat.

tips.text: Keep the back flat as you hinge forward.
Lift the toes to feel the hamstring stretch.
Inhale to stand tall, exhale to hinge forward.
Open both arms upward as much as you can while hinging forward.
This exercise stretches the hamstrings and opens the chest.

3426.name: TAI CHI FLOWING STEP
3426.introduce:
Stand tall and lift your arms overhead from the sides, bringing your palms together.

Exhale, step your left foot out to the side into a wide squat stance while lowering your arms to your sides.

Inhale, bring your foot and hands back to the start position.

Switch sides and repeat in a smooth rhythm.

tips.text: Keep your chest lifted and shoulders relaxed.
Inhale as the arms rise, exhale as they lower.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes during the squat.
This exercise targets your arms and legs.

3428.name: CLOUD HANDS
3428.introduce:
Stand as wide as comfortable and sink into a horse stance with the knees aligned over the toes.

Exhale, turn your torso to the left, and raise your left hand at eye level while keeping your right hand lower, palm facing up, as if cradling the moon.

Inhale, smoothly switch hand positions. Then, rotate your torso to the right, continuing this flowing motion.

Imagine your hands gliding through clouds as they move in gentle circles.

tips.text: Inhale as you switch your hands, and exhale as you twist your torso.
Let your waist guide the movement.
Keep your spine tall and your shoulders relaxed.
This exercise strengthens your core, arms, and legs.

3430.name: KNEE CIRCLE MOBILITY
3430.introduce: Start in a partial squat with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your hands resting on your knees.\n\nBreathe naturally and move your knees outward in a circular motion.

tips.text: Keep the circles small and smooth.
Keep the spine neutral and the upper body steady.
Take slow breaths through each circle.
This exercise improves knee mobility and warms the lower body.

3431.name: RELAXING SHAKE
3431.introduce:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Place your hands in front of your waist, palms facing upward, as if holding a ball.

Gently lift and lower your heels while allowing your shoulders to move with the rhythm, creating a full-body shake from head to toe.

Breathe naturally and feel the body relax with each shake.

tips.text: Let the whole body shake freely.
Breathe naturally.
This is a good warm-up exercise.
This exercise helps strengthen your legs.

3432.name: SIDE STEP OPEN & CLOSE
3432.introduce:
Stand with knees slightly bent and arms relaxed at your sides.

As you rise, step your left foot to the side while opening your arms at shoulder height. Inhale to lower your arms and step back to the center.

Exhale, step your right foot to the side, opening your elbows out to shoulder height with your fists in front of your chest.

Return to the starting position and repeat with a smooth rhythm.

tips.text: Engage your core to stay stable.
Exhale as you step out, inhale as you return to the center.
Avoid shifting your weight from side to side.
This exercise activates your legs, shoulders, and arms.

3433.name: SIDE TAP & EXTEND
3433.introduce:
Stand upright with your hands on your waist.

Exhale, step your left foot to the side, and lightly tap the floor with your toes while rotating your left forearm up.

Inhale, return to the starting position, then switch sides to repeat.

Keep your weight centered throughout the movement.

tips.text: Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Exhale as you step out, inhale as you return to the center.
Avoid shifting your weight from side to side.
This exercise strengthens your legs and shoulders.

3434.name: GOLDEN ROOSTER BALANCE
3434.introduce:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and the knees slightly bent.

As you rise, exhale and lift your left knee while pressing your left palm upward.

Inhale as you return to the starting position, then repeat on the other side.

tips.text: Perform the movement slowly and with control.
Engage your core to stay stable.
Fix your gaze on a single point ahead to help keep balance.
Exhale to lift the knee, inhale to lower it.
Use a chair or wall for support if you feel unsteady.
This exercise builds balance and core stability.
This exercise helps activate your legs and hip flexors.

3437.name: EASY IN-PLACE JOG
3437.introduce:
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.

Alternately lift your heels while keeping your toes on the floor, swinging your arms naturally in coordination with your steps.

Breathe naturally throughout.

tips.text: Land lightly on your heels.
Swing your arms in coordination with your steps.
Engage your core to stay stable.
Breathe naturally throughout.
This exercise warms the whole body and boosts circulation.
This exercise activates the legs.

3440.name: FLYING WING BOUNCE
3440.introduce:
Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width apart and arms lifted out to the sides with elbows slightly bent.

Alternately raise the left and right knees as you flap your arms up and down like wings.

Keep the movement soft and flowing while breathing naturally.

tips.text: Keep the elbows softly bent — don't lock the arms.
Keep the movement smooth and flowing.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise activates the legs, shoulders, and chest.
This exercise helps improve coordination and balance.

29.name: SIDE PLANK RIGHT
29.introduce: Lie on your right side with your forearm supporting your body. Hold your body in a straight line. \n\nThis exercise targets the abdominal muscles and obliques.

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your arm at a 90 degree angle.
Keep your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Open your chest.
Always keep your body straight.
Put pressure on your wrist and elbow.
Don't put pressure on your shoulders.
Breathe regularly.
To make it easier, put your top foot forward on the mat.
Your abdominals will be burning, maybe even shivering.
Your shoulder should not be sore.
This exercise can strengthen your core.

35.name: SIDE PLANK LEFT
35.introduce: Lie on your left side with your forearm supporting your body. Hold your body in a straight line. \n\nThis exercise targets the abdominal muscles and obliques.

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your arm at a 90 degree angle.
Keep your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Open your chest.
Always keep your body straight.
Put pressure on your wrist and elbow.
Don't put pressure on your shoulders.
Breathe regularly.
To make it easier, put your top foot forward on the mat.
Your abdominals will be burning, maybe even shivering.
Your shoulder should not be sore.
This exercise can strengthen your core.

451.name: MOUNTAIN CLIMBER
451.introduce: Start in the push-up position. Bend your right knee towards your chest and keep your left leg straight, then quickly switch from one leg to the other. \n\nThis exercise strengthens multiple muscle groups.

tips.text: We suggest you do this on a mat.
Bring your knees as close to your chest as possible.
Don't lift your hips up.
Take steady and deep breaths.
If you feel it's too easy, do it as fast as you can.
If you feel it's too hard, adjust to a speed that makes you feel comfortable.
If you feel it's too hard, elevate your hands on a bench.
This is a great full body exercise.
This can strengthen your cardiovascular system.

493.name: FROG PUMP
493.introduce:
Lie on your back with your legs bent and feet together. 

Bend your elbows at your sides, and dig them into the ground for support. 

Spread your knees to your sides and lift your hips up and down.

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please squeeze your glutes when lifting.
Please slightly lift your head and tuck your chin.
Exhale as you raise your hips and inhale as you lower them.
Please keep your abs tight during the exercise.
It's a good exercise for glutes activation.
